doc.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022

title: Mixing and the first playback
summary: Asked who he wanted in the booth for mixing, Hank stresses the first playback and a good earphone mix.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: How about when it comes to mixing? Who did you like to have in the booth when it came time for mixing, or who didn’t you want to have in the booth?

I never had too much trouble with that. I mean if you’ve got a producer you have a producer. If the artist is producing, as long as you give them that first playback where they’re comfortable and their ears are comfortable it makes it easier for you. You know that first playback when you do a tune and they’re working out there for an hour and a half you get in front of it, you make three or four takes and they come in and listen, you’ve got to be right on it. You know you’ve got to figure out before they even set up sometimes who’s the lead artist, who’s the lead guitar, whatever. You get a good drum sound. Earphones are important. With the right earphone mix, like I would some days say, “Don’t put on the phones yet” and I would get as much as I could out of the date and then I would go to the earphones and work really carefully on the earphone and then ask the guys, “Are you comfortable? Your earphones are right?” If the earphones are right and they’re hearing a nice mix in their phones, man, your job is a lot easier.
